payload.headline: Netflix edges toward support; growth slowing, estimates cut; still waiting for 61.63

summary.thesis: Netflix is a solid, cash-rich business (grade B) priced below most of its fair-value estimates, but sales growth is slowing, profit margins are at a peak and the chart is weak, so the price has little room for error until it reaches support.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, then start buying in the 61.15–61.63 support zone and add near 60.37. Swing: no trade until the stock holds support or closes back above resistance.

payload.happening: Netflix closed at 62.15, down 0.86% on the day. It is about one point above the 61.15–61.63 support zone and below all three of its moving averages (20-day 64.34, 50-day 69.18, 200-day 80.5), and all three are falling. There has been no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-19.
payload.business: The business itself is still growing and making plenty of cash. Revenue over the last twelve months was 49.7B, up from 43.4B. Free cash flow (the cash left after running and investing in the business) was 11.4B, up from 9.0B. The operating margin (the share of sales kept as operating profit) rose to 31.3% from 29.14%, and the share count fell 3.35% over the year because of buybacks. What is at risk is how fast it grows and how long the margin lasts. Quarterly sales growth has slowed to 11.85%, from 16.19% two quarters ago. The filings note that a 31% margin sits at the top of its 5-year range (17–31%) and that peaks like this usually fade. Analysts keep trimming their forecasts: this quarter's EPS estimate (earnings per share) is 7.3% lower than 30 days ago, and the 30-day revision across estimates is -1.11%. Debt exceeds cash by 4.4B (net cash -4.4B), which is manageable next to 11.4B of yearly free cash flow. The falling chart and the cautious macro view (tech market in a downtrend) affect sentiment, not demand. There is no reported news that changes the competitive picture.

worth.text: At 62.15, Netflix trades at 17.7 times trailing earnings and 16.5 times next year's expected earnings. Its price-to-sales ratio is 5.1, compared with a peer median of 7.2, and that ratio sits at the 23rd percentile of its own 5-year history, so it is cheap against both its peers and its past. The discounted-cash-flow model (DCF: today's value of future cash) gives 38.33 bear, 65.31 base and 78.29 bull. The stock's own price-to-sales history gives 60.37 to 122.15. The gap between methods comes down to one assumption: how fast free cash flow grows from here. The current price implies starting growth of about 13.8%. At 10% starting growth the value is 53.25. At 20% it is 79.46. Margins are the second lever. If the operating margin fell to 23%, the value would drop to 59.33, which is below today's price. The price is therefore fair to slightly cheap, but not a bargain while growth is slowing.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow keeps growing at about the 13.8% the price implies, even though quarterly sales growth has slowed to 11.85% and the margin sits at a 5-year peak.

bull: Price-to-sales of 5.1 is well below the peer median of 7.2 and at the 23rd percentile of its own 5-year history.
Free cash flow grew to 11.4B from 9.0B, and buybacks cut the share count by 3.35% over the year.
The operating margin rose to 31.3% from 29.14%, and the DCF base value of 65.31 sits above the 62.15 close.
bear: Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago.
This quarter's EPS estimate fell 7.3% in 30 days, from 0.73 to 0.68.
If the peak 31% margin fades to 23%, the value falls to 59.33, below today's price.

levels.what: Top of the 61.15–61.63 support zone, where to start building a position
Low end of the own-history price-to-sales range, close to the 60 put strike with the most open interest (37723), where to add
DCF base value; above it, the margin of safety is gone, so no buying there

longterm.why: The business quality is good and the stock is cheap against its history and peers. But estimates are still being cut and the margin is at a peak, so the plan is to buy only at support, where a margin fade to the 59.33 case does less damage.

swing.why: The trend is down: lower highs and lower lows, and price is below three falling averages. There is no trade until the stock either holds 61.15–61.63 or closes above the 20-day average of 64.34 and resistance at 64.84–65.32.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-01-19 come after the 2027-01-15 option expiry, and options price a move of about 11.8% by that date. With estimates still falling, any buying before the report should be small and limited to the support zone.

change_mind: A close below 60.37 (the own-history low), together with another cut to next year's EPS estimate (now 3.77), would mean the selling is about the business, not just sentiment. That would move the decision to avoid until the 2027-01-19 report.
A close above the 66.54–67.49 resistance zone would break the pattern of lower highs and turn the swing view to enter.
If the 2027-01-19 report shows quarterly sales growth below 11.85% and an operating margin below 29.14%, the margin-fade case (59.33 at a 23% margin) becomes the base case.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait for the 61.15–61.63 zone; the 62.15 close is closer to it but still above it, so the buy level has not been reached.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
